title.en: Volume 42 Biographies 34: Yang Fei; Lu Qian (Northern Qi); Cui Jie (Northern Qi); Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu
title.raw: 卷四二 列傳第三四 陽斐 盧潛 崔劼 盧叔武 陽休之 袁聿修 Volume 42 Biographies 34: Yang Fei; Lu Qian (Northern Qi); Cui Jie (Northern Qi); Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu

sentences.zh: 陽斐 盧潛 崔劼 盧叔武 陽休之 袁聿修

translations.literal: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu (陽斐 盧潛 崔劼 盧叔武 陽休之 袁聿修)
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fei; Lu Qian; Cui Jie; Lu Shuowu; Yang Xiuzhi; Yuan Yuxiu

sentences.zh: 陽斐，字叔鸞，北平漁陽人也。

translations.literal: Yang Fei, styled Shuluan, was a man of Yuyang in Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Fei, styled Shuluan, came from Yuyang in Beiping.

sentences.zh: 父藻，魏建德太守，贈幽州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Zao was Wei administrator of Jiande; posthumously enfeoffed as inspector of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zao had been Wei administrator of Jiande and was posthumously enfeoffed as inspector of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 孝莊時，斐於西兗督護流民有功，賜爵方城伯。

translations.literal: In the Xiaozhuang era, Fei had merit supervising displaced populations in Western Yan and was enfeoffed as Baron of Fangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaozhuang of Wei, Fei had merit supervising displaced populations in Western Yan and was enfeoffed as baron of Fangcheng.

sentences.zh: 歷侍御史，兼都官郎中、廣平王開府中郎，修《起居注》。

translations.literal: He served in succession as attendant censor, concurrently director of the office for capital cases, establishment-office middle aide to Prince of Guangping, and compiler of the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as attendant censor, concurrently as director of the office for capital cases and middle aide in Prince of Guangping's establishment office, and as compiler of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 興和中，除起部郎中，兼通直散騎常侍，聘於梁。

translations.literal: In the Xinghe era he was made director of the ministry of appointments, concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and sent on embassy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xinghe era he was made director of the ministry of appointments, concurrently regular attendant of the scattered cavalry, and sent on embassy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 梁尚書羊侃，魏之叛人也，與斐有舊，欲請斐至宅，三致書，斐不答。

translations.literal: Liang Minister of Writing Yang Kan was a Wei defector who had old ties with Fei and wished to invite Fei to his house; he sent three letters, and Fei did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Liang minister of writing Yang Kan was a Wei defector with old ties to Fei and wished to invite him to his house. He sent three letters; Fei did not reply.

sentences.zh: 梁人曰：「羊來已久，經貴朝遷革，李、盧亦詣宅相見，卿何致難？

translations.literal: The Liang people said: "Yang has been here a long time, and through your noble dynasty's changes Li and Lu also called at his house to meet him—why do you make it difficult?
translations.idiomatic: The Liang people said, "Yang has been here a long time. Through your noble dynasty's changes, Li and Lu also called at his house—why do you make it difficult?

sentences.zh: 」斐曰：「柳下惠則可，吾不可。

translations.literal: " Fei said: "What Lianghui did, he might do; I may not.
translations.idiomatic: " Fei said, "What Lianghui did, he might do; I may not.

sentences.zh: 」梁主乃親謂斐曰：「羊侃極願相見，今二國和好，天下一家，安得復論彼此。

translations.literal: " The Liang ruler then personally told Fei: "Yang Kan ardently wishes to meet you. Now the two states are on good terms and all under Heaven is one family—how can we again speak of this side and that?
translations.idiomatic: " The Liang ruler then told Fei in person, "Yang Kan ardently wishes to meet you. Now the two states are on good terms and all under Heaven is one family—how can we again speak of this side and that?

sentences.zh: 」斐終辭焉。

translations.literal: " In the end Fei declined.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end Fei declined.

sentences.zh: 使還，除廷尉少卿。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he was made vice director of the court of justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the mission returned he was made vice director of the court of justice.

sentences.zh: 石濟河溢，橋壞，斐修治之。

translations.literal: The Stone Ford River overflowed and the bridge was ruined; Fei repaired it.
translations.idiomatic: The Stone Ford River overflowed and the bridge was ruined; Fei repaired it.

sentences.zh: 又移津於白馬，中河起石潬，兩岸造關城，累年乃就。

translations.literal: He also moved the ford to White Horse, raised stone weirs in mid-river, and built pass-cities on both banks—a project of many years before it was finished.
translations.idiomatic: He also moved the ford to White Horse, raised stone weirs in mid-river, and built pass-cities on both banks. The work took many years to finish.

sentences.zh: 東郡太守陸士佩以黎陽關河形勝，欲因山卽壑以為公家苑囿。

translations.literal: Administrator of Dong commandery Lu Shipei, because Liyang Pass and the river terrain were strategically strong, wished to follow the mountains and ravines to make a public park and hunting preserve.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shipei, administrator of Dong commandery, because Liyang Pass and the river terrain were strategically strong, wished to follow the mountains and ravines and make a public park and hunting preserve.

sentences.zh: 遺斐書曰：「當諮大將軍，以足下為匠者。

translations.literal: He sent Fei a letter saying: "I shall consult the Grand General and make you the craftsman."
translations.idiomatic: He sent Fei a letter saying, "I shall consult the grand general and make you the craftsman."

sentences.zh: 」斐答書拒曰：「當今殷憂啟聖，運遭昌歷。

translations.literal: Fei answered refusing: "At present deep sorrow has awakened a sage, and fortune meets a flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: Fei answered in refusal: "At present deep sorrow has awakened a sage, and fortune meets a flourishing age.

sentences.zh: 故大丞相天啟霸功，再造太極；

translations.literal: Hence the late Grand Chancellor, Heaven opening his hegemonic achievement, remade the Supreme Ultimate;
translations.idiomatic: Hence the late grand chancellor Gao Huan, Heaven opening his hegemonic achievement, remade the supreme pole;

sentences.zh: 大將軍光承先構，嗣績丕顯。

translations.literal: the Grand General, light inheriting the prior structure, continuing the great enterprise manifestly bright.
translations.idiomatic: the grand general Gao Cheng, light inheriting the prior structure, continuing the great enterprise in manifest brightness.

sentences.zh: 國步始康，民勞未息，誠宜輕徭薄賦，勤恤民隱。

translations.literal: The state's steps have just grown secure and the people's toil is not yet eased—truly one ought to lighten corvée and reduce levies and diligently tend the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: The state's steps have just grown secure and the people's toil is not yet eased—truly one ought to lighten corvée, reduce levies, and diligently tend the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 《詩》不云乎：『民亦勞止，迄可小康，惠此中國，以綏四方。

translations.literal: Does not the Odes say: 'The people also are weary; they may have a little rest—show favor to these central lands and thereby pacify the four quarters.'
translations.idiomatic: Does not the Odes say, 'The people also are weary; they may have a little rest—show favor to these central lands and thereby pacify the four quarters.'

sentences.zh: 』古之帝王，亦有表山刊樹，未足盡其意；

translations.literal: The ancient emperors also had times when they marked out mountains and carved trees, yet that fell short of fulfilling their intent;
translations.idiomatic: The ancient emperors also marked out mountains and carved trees, yet that fell short of fulfilling their intent;

sentences.zh: 下輦成宴，詎能窮其情。

translations.literal: alighted from the chariot to hold a feast—how could that exhaust their feeling?
translations.idiomatic: they alighted from the chariot to hold a feast—how could that exhaust their feeling?

sentences.zh: 正足以靡天地之財用，剝生民之髓腦。

translations.literal: It only sufficed to waste Heaven-and-Earth's wealth and pare the living people's marrow and brain.
translations.idiomatic: It only wasted Heaven-and-Earth's wealth and pared the living people's marrow and brain.

sentences.zh: 是故孔子對葉公以來遠，酬哀公以臨民，所問雖同，所急異務故也。

translations.literal: Therefore Confucius answered Duke Ye of Chu on welcoming the distant and replied to Duke Ai of Lu on caring for the people—the questions were alike yet the urgent tasks differed.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Confucius answered Duke Ye of Chu on welcoming the distant and replied to Duke Ai of Lu on caring for the people—the questions were alike, yet the urgent tasks differed.

sentences.zh: 相如壯上林之觀，揚雄騁羽獵之辭，雖系以頹墻填塹，亂以收罝落網，而言無補於風規，只足昭其愆戾也。」

translations.literal: Xiangru exalted the Shanglin spectacle, Yang Xiong deployed the feather-hunt rhetoric—though tied off with crumbling walls and filled dikes, and set among gathering nets and falling game—yet the words did not aid wind and teaching; they only enough declared their excess and fault."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiangru exalted the Shanglin spectacle and Yang Xiong deployed the feather-hunt rhetoric—though tied off with crumbling walls and filled dikes, and set among gathering nets and falling game—the words did not aid wind and teaching; they only declared excess and fault."

sentences.zh: 盧潛，范陽涿人也。

translations.literal: Lu Qian was a man of Zhuo in Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian came from Zhuo in Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 祖尚之，魏濟州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shangzhi was Wei inspector of Ji province.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shangzhi was Wei inspector of Ji province.

sentences.zh: 父文符，通直侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Wenfu was regular attendant for direct communication.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenfu was regular attendant for direct communication.

sentences.zh: 潛容貌瑰偉，善言談，少有成人志尚。

translations.literal: Qian's appearance was striking and grand; he was skilled in conversation and from youth had the aspiration and bearing of a mature man.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's appearance was striking and grand. He was skilled in conversation and from youth had the aspiration and bearing of a mature man.

sentences.zh: 儀同賀拔勝辟開府行參軍，補侍御史。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Equal He Ba Sheng recruited him as expeditionary aide in the establishment office; he was made up as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendant equal He Ba Sheng recruited him as expeditionary aide in the establishment office; he was made up as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 世宗引為大將軍西閤祭酒，轉中外府中兵參軍，機事強濟，為世宗所知，言其終可大用。

translations.literal: Gao Cheng drew him in as western-pavilion libationer for the general-in-chief, transferred to middle military aide in the inner-and-outer office, strong and effective in confidential matters, known to Gao Cheng, who said he would in the end be greatly useful.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Cheng drew him in as western-pavilion libationer for the general-in-chief and transferred him to middle military aide in the inner-and-outer office. He was strong and effective in confidential matters and came to Gao Cheng's notice; Gao Cheng said he would in the end be greatly useful.

sentences.zh: 王思政見獲於潁川，世宗重其才識。

translations.literal: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Gao Cheng valued his talent and insight.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sizheng was captured at Yingchuan; Gao Cheng valued his talent and insight.

sentences.zh: 潛曾從容白世宗云：「思政不能死節，何足可重！

translations.literal: Qian once at leisure told Gao Cheng: "Sizheng could not die defending principle—how is he worth esteeming!
translations.idiomatic: Qian once told Gao Cheng at leisure, "Sizheng could not die defending principle—how is he worth esteeming!

sentences.zh: 」世宗謂左右曰：「我有盧潛，便是更得一王思政。

translations.literal: " Gao Cheng told those at his side: "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."
translations.idiomatic: " Gao Cheng told those at his side, "With Lu Qian I have gained another Wang Sizheng."

sentences.zh: 」天保初，除中書舍人，以奏事忤旨免。

translations.literal: Early in Tianbao he was made secretariat gentleman; for memorial matters offensive to the ruler's intent he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Tianbao he was made secretariat gentleman; for memorial matters that offended the ruler's intent he was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 尋除左民郎中，坐譏議《魏書》，與王松年、李庶等俱被禁止。

translations.literal: Soon he was made left-director gentleman in the ministry of the people; for criticizing the Wei History he was confined together with Wang Songnian, Li Shu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made left-director gentleman in the ministry of the people. For criticizing the Wei History he was confined together with Wang Songnian, Li Shu, and others.

sentences.zh: 會清河王岳將救江陵，特赦潛以為岳行臺郎。

translations.literal: When Prince of Qinghe Yue was about to rescue Jiangling, Qian was specially amnestied and made Yue's mobile-staff aide.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Qinghe Yue was about to rescue Jiangling, Qian was specially amnestied and made Yue's mobile-staff aide.

sentences.zh: 還，遷中書侍郎，尋遷黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: On return he was moved to secretariat vice director; soon he was moved to vice director of the yellow gate.
translations.idiomatic: On return he was moved to secretariat vice director; soon he was moved to vice director of the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 黃門鄭子默奏言，潛從清河王南討，清河王令潛說梁將侯瑱，大納賂遺，還不奏聞。

translations.literal: Yellow-gate gentleman Zheng Zimo memorialized that when Qian followed Prince of Qinghe on the southern campaign, the prince had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian, who took large bribes, and on return did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow-gate gentleman Zheng Zimo memorialized that when Qian followed Prince of Qinghe on the southern campaign, the prince had Qian persuade Liang general Hou Tian, who took large bribes, and on return did not report it.

sentences.zh: 顯祖杖潛一百，仍截其鬚，左遷魏尹丞。

translations.literal: Gao Yang caned Qian one hundred strokes, still cut off his beard, and demoted him to aide of the metropolitan magistrate of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Yang caned Qian one hundred strokes, still cut off his beard, and demoted him to aide of the metropolitan magistrate of Wei.

sentences.zh: 尋除司州別駕，出為江州刺史，所在有治方。

translations.literal: Soon he was made separate aide of the inspector of Si province, went out as inspector of Jiang province, and wherever he served had methods of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made separate aide of the inspector of Si province, then went out as inspector of Jiang province; wherever he served he had methods of governance.

sentences.zh: 肅宗作相，以潛為揚州道行臺左丞。

translations.literal: Gao Yan served as chancellor; Qian was made left aide on the Yangzhou circuit mobile staff.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yan served as chancellor, Qian was made left aide on the Yangzhou circuit mobile staff.

sentences.zh: 先是梁將王琳為陳兵所敗，擁其主蕭莊歸壽陽，朝廷以琳為揚州刺史，勑潛與琳為南討經略。

translations.literal: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had been defeated by Chen troops, escorting his lord Xiao Zhuang back to Shouyang; the court made Lin inspector of Yangzhou and ordered Qian together with Lin to conduct southern-campaign strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liang general Wang Lin had been defeated by Chen troops and escorted his lord Xiao Zhuang back to Shouyang. The court made Lin inspector of Yangzhou and ordered Qian together with Lin to conduct southern-campaign strategy.

sentences.zh: 琳部曲義故多在揚州，與陳寇鄰接。

translations.literal: Lin's old troops and adherents were mostly in Yangzhou, adjoining Chen invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Lin's old troops and adherents were mostly in Yangzhou, adjoining Chen invaders.

sentences.zh: 潛輯諧內外，甚得邊俗之和。

translations.literal: Qian brought internal and external into harmony and deeply won the border people's accord.
translations.idiomatic: Qian brought internal and external affairs into harmony and deeply won the border people's accord.

sentences.zh: 陳秦、譙二州刺史王奉國、合州刺史周令珍前後入寇，潛輒破平之，以功加散騎常侍，食彭城郡幹。

translations.literal: Chen inspectors of Qin and Qiao prefectures Wang Fengguo and of He prefecture Zhou Lingzhen invaded in succession; Qian at once defeated and pacified them; for merit he was given added rank as scattered-cavalry regular attendant with salary from Pengcheng commandery dry fief.
translations.idiomatic: Chen inspectors of Qin and Qiao prefectures Wang Fengguo and of He prefecture Zhou Lingzhen invaded in succession; Qian at once defeated and pacified them. For merit he was given added rank as scattered-cavalry regular attendant with salary from the dry fief of Pengcheng commandery.

sentences.zh: 遷合州刺史，左丞如故。

translations.literal: He was moved to inspector of He province while continuing as left aide.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to inspector of He province while continuing as left aide.

sentences.zh: 又除行臺尚書，尋授儀同三司。

translations.literal: He was again made mobile-staff director of the masters of writing; soon he was given acting insignia equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made mobile-staff director of the masters of writing; soon he was given acting insignia equal to the three excellencies.

sentences.zh: 王琳銳意圖南，潛以為時事未可。

translations.literal: Wang Lin was keen to scheme south; Qian thought the times were not yet ripe.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Lin was keen to scheme south; Qian thought the times were not yet ripe.

sentences.zh: 屬陳遣移書至壽陽，請與國家和好。

translations.literal: It happened that Chen sent a letter to Shouyang requesting peace and harmony with the state.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that Chen sent a letter to Shouyang requesting peace and harmony with the state.

sentences.zh: 潛為奏聞，仍上啟且願息兵。

translations.literal: Qian memorialized the report and also submitted a memorial wishing to cease arms.
translations.idiomatic: Qian memorialized the report and also submitted a memorial wishing to cease arms.

sentences.zh: 依所請。

translations.literal: As requested.
translations.idiomatic: As requested.

sentences.zh: 由是與琳有隙，更相表列。

translations.literal: Because of this he and Lin were at odds, mutually impeaching each other in memorials.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this he and Lin were at odds and mutually impeached each other in memorials.

sentences.zh: 世祖追琳入京，除潛揚州刺史，領行臺尚書。

translations.literal: Gao Zhan recalled Lin to the capital and made Qian inspector of Yangzhou, still holding mobile-staff director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Zhan recalled Lin to the capital and made Qian inspector of Yangzhou, still holding mobile-staff director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 潛在淮南十三年，任總軍民，大樹風績，甚為陳人所憚。

translations.literal: Qian was in Huainan thirteen years, in overall charge of army and people, planting great achievements; Chen men deeply feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian was in Huainan thirteen years, in overall charge of army and people, and planted great achievements; Chen men deeply feared him.

sentences.zh: 陳主與其邊將書云：「盧潛猶在壽陽，聞其何當還北，此虜不死，方為國患，卿宜深備之。

translations.literal: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals: "Lu Qian is still at Shouyang—heard when will he return north? While this captive is not dead he will be a national calamity; you ought to guard deeply against him."
translations.idiomatic: The Chen ruler wrote his frontier generals, "Lu Qian is still at Shouyang—when will he return north? While this captive is not dead he will be a national calamity; you ought to guard deeply against him."

sentences.zh: 」顯祖初平淮南，給十年優復。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Gao Yang pacified Huainan he granted ten years of privileged exemption from levies.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning, when Gao Yang pacified Huainan, he granted ten years of privileged exemption from levies.

sentences.zh: 年滿之後，逮天統、武平中，徵稅煩雜。

translations.literal: After the term ended, by the Tiantong and Wuping eras taxation grew numerous and complex.
translations.idiomatic: After the term ended, by the Tiantong and Wuping eras taxation grew numerous and complex.

sentences.zh: 又高元海執政，斷漁獵，人家無以自資。

translations.literal: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and prohibited fishing and hunting so households had no means to support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Gao Yuanhai held power and prohibited fishing and hunting, so households had no means to support themselves.

sentences.zh: 諸商胡負官責息者，宦者陳德信縱其妄注淮南富家，令州縣徵責。

translations.literal: Various merchant Hu who owed official interest were allowed by eunuch Chen Dexin arbitrarily to register the debts against wealthy families of Huainan and order prefectures and counties to collect payment.
translations.idiomatic: Various merchant Hu who owed official interest were allowed by eunuch Chen Dexin arbitrarily to register the debts against wealthy Huainan families and order prefectures and counties to collect payment.

sentences.zh: 又勑送突厥馬數千疋於揚州管內，令土豪貴買之。

translations.literal: There was also an edict to send several thousand Turkish horses into Yangzhou's jurisdiction and order local magnates to buy them at high price.
translations.idiomatic: There was also an edict to send several thousand Turkish horses into Yangzhou's jurisdiction and order local magnates to buy them at high price.

sentences.zh: 錢直始入，便出勑括江、淮間馬，並送官廄。

translations.literal: The money had scarcely entered when an edict came to seize horses throughout the Jiang and Huai region and send them all to the government stables.
translations.idiomatic: The money had scarcely entered when an edict came to seize horses throughout the Jiang and Huai region and send them all to the government stables.

sentences.zh: 由是百姓騷擾，切齒嗟怨。

translations.literal: Because of this the common people were disturbed; they gnashed teeth and sighed in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the common people were disturbed; they gnashed their teeth and sighed in resentment.

sentences.zh: 潛隨事撫慰，兼行權略，故得寧靖。

translations.literal: Qian according to circumstances comforted them and also employed expedient strategy, and therefore attained peace.
translations.idiomatic: Qian according to circumstances comforted them and also employed expedient strategy, and therefore attained peace.

sentences.zh: 武平三年，徵為五兵尚書。

translations.literal: In the third Wuping year he was summoned as director of the five armies ministry.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Wuping year he was summoned as director of the five armies ministry.

sentences.zh: 揚州吏民以潛戒斷酒肉，篤信釋氏，大設僧會，以香華緣道，流涕送之。

translations.literal: Yangzhou officials and people, because Qian strictly avoided wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held a great Buddhist assembly, with incense and flowers lining the road, and sent him off weeping.
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou officials and people, because Qian strictly avoided wine and meat and devoutly believed in Buddhism, held a great Buddhist assembly, with incense and flowers lining the road, and sent him off weeping.

sentences.zh: 潛嘆曰：「正恐不久復來耳。

translations.literal: Qian sighed: "I fear not long before I return."
translations.idiomatic: Qian sighed, "I fear not long before I return."

sentences.zh: 」至鄴未幾，陳將吳明徹渡江侵掠，復以潛為揚州道行臺尚書。

translations.literal: At Ye not many days had passed when Chen general Wu Mingche crossed the river invading; Qian was again made Yangzhou-circuit mobile-staff director of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: At Ye, not many days had passed when Chen general Wu Mingche crossed the river invading; Qian was again made Yangzhou-circuit mobile-staff director of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 五年，與王琳等同陷。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he fell together with Wang Lin and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he fell together with Wang Lin and the rest.

sentences.zh: 尋死建業，年五十七。

translations.literal: Soon he died at Jianye, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he died at Jianye, aged fifty-seven.

sentences.zh: 其家購屍歸葬。

translations.literal: His family ransomed the corpse to return for burial.
translations.idiomatic: His family ransomed the corpse to return it for burial.

sentences.zh: 贈開府儀同三司、尚書右僕射、兗州刺史。

translations.literal: Posthumously enfeoffed as grand master opening the government with protocol equal to the Three Excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and inspector of Yan province.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously enfeoffed as grand master opening the government with protocol equal to the three excellencies, right vice director of the masters of writing, and inspector of Yan province.

sentences.zh: 無子，以弟士邃子元孝為嗣。

translations.literal: Having no sons, he took his younger brother Shisui's son Yuanxiao as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Having no sons, he took his younger brother Shisui's son Yuanxiao as heir.

sentences.zh: 士邃，字子淹，少為崔昂所知，昂云：「此昆季足為後生之俊，但恨其俱不讀書耳。

translations.literal: Shisui, styled Ziyan, in youth was known to Cui Ang; Ang said: "These brothers are enough to be outstanding men of the younger generation—only a pity they do not read books at all."
translations.idiomatic: Shisui, styled Ziyan, in youth was known to Cui Ang. Ang said, "These brothers are enough to be outstanding men of the younger generation—only a pity they do not read books at all."

sentences.zh: 」歷侍御史、司徒祭酒、尚書郎、鄴縣令、尚書左右丞、吏部郎中，出為中山太守，帶定州長史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as attendant censor, libationer of the ministry of worship, gentleman of the masters of writing, magistrate of Ye county, left and right vice directors of the masters of writing, director in the ministry of personnel; went out as administrator of Zhongshan, concurrently chief administrator of Ding province.
translations.idiomatic: He served in succession as attendant censor, libationer of the ministry of worship, gentleman of the masters of writing, magistrate of Ye county, left and right vice directors of the masters of writing, and director in the ministry of personnel; he went out as administrator of Zhongshan, concurrently chief administrator of Ding province.

sentences.zh: 齊亡後卒。

translations.literal: After Qi fell he died.
translations.idiomatic: After Qi fell he died.

sentences.zh: 潛從祖兄懷仁，字子友，魏司徒司馬道將之子。

translations.literal: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's second cousin Huainian, styled Ziyou, was son of Wei secretariat marshal Daojiang.

sentences.zh: 懷仁涉學有文辭，情性恬靖，常蕭然有閑放之致。

translations.literal: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.
translations.idiomatic: Huainian was broadly learned with literary accomplishment; his nature was calm and quiet, often bearing an air of leisurely detachment.

sentences.zh: 歷太尉記室、弘農郡守，不之任，卜居陳留界。

translations.literal: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: He served as recorder for the grand commandant and as administrator of Hongnong but did not take up the post, choosing residence on the border of Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 所著詩賦銘頌二萬餘言，又撰《中表實錄》二十卷。

translations.literal: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: His writings in poetry, fu, eulogy, and hymn exceeded twenty thousand words; he also compiled Records of Kindred Excellence in twenty scrolls.

sentences.zh: 懷仁有行檢，善與人交，與瑯邪王衍、隴西李壽之情好相得。

translations.literal: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.
translations.idiomatic: Huainian had conduct and probity and was good at friendship; with Langye Wang Yan and Longxi Li Shou he was deeply close.

sentences.zh: 曾語衍云：「昔太丘道廣，許劭知而不顧；

translations.literal: He once told Yan: "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;
translations.idiomatic: He once told Yan, "In antiquity Taichiu's way was broad yet Xu Shao knew him and would not look at him;

sentences.zh: 嵇生性惰，鐘會過而絕言。

translations.literal: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.
translations.idiomatic: Ji's nature was indolent yet Zhong Hui passed by and broke off speech with him.

sentences.zh: 吾處季、孟之間，去其泰甚。

translations.literal: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."
translations.idiomatic: I stand between Chi and Meng and have removed their excesses."

sentences.zh: 」愆以為然。

translations.literal: Yan thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: Yan thought it so.

sentences.zh: 武平末卒。

translations.literal: He died late in Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: He died late in Wuping.

sentences.zh: 懷仁兄子莊之，少有名望。

translations.literal: Huainian's elder brother's son Zhuangzhi in youth had name and repute.
translations.idiomatic: Huainian's elder brother's son Zhuangzhi in youth had name and repute.

sentences.zh: 官歷太子舍人、定州別駕、東平太守。

translations.literal: He held office as crown-prince gentleman attendant, separate aide of Ding province, administrator of Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: He held office as crown-prince gentleman attendant, separate aide of Ding province, and administrator of Dongping.

sentences.zh: 武平中都水使者，卒官。

translations.literal: Late in Wuping he was commissioner of waterways; he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was commissioner of waterways; he died in office.

sentences.zh: 懷仁從父弟昌衡，魏尚書左僕射道虔之子。

translations.literal: Huainian's younger cousin from father's line Changheng was son of Wei left vice director of the masters of writing Daogian.
translations.idiomatic: Huainian's younger cousin from his father's line Changheng was son of Wei left vice director of the masters of writing Daogian.

sentences.zh: 武平末尚書郎。

translations.literal: Late in Wuping he was gentleman of the masters of writing.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was gentleman of the masters of writing.

sentences.zh: 沉靖有才識，風儀蘊籍，容止可觀。

translations.literal: Calm and quiet with talent and insight, bearing and manner well contained, deportment worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: Calm and quiet with talent and insight, bearing and manner well contained, deportment worth viewing.

sentences.zh: 天保中，尚書王昕以雅談獲罪，諸弟尚守而不墜，自茲以後，此道頓微。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era Minister of Writing Wang Xin was condemned for elegant talk; his younger brothers still maintained it but thereafter this way suddenly declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianbao era minister of writing Wang Xin was condemned for elegant talk; his younger brothers still maintained it, but thereafter this way suddenly declined.

sentences.zh: 昌衡與頓丘李若、彭城劉泰瑉、河南陸彥師、隴西辛德源、太原王脩並為後進風流之士。

translations.literal: Changheng together with Dunqiu Li Ruo, Pengcheng Liu Taizhen, Henan Lu Yanshi, Longxi Xin Deyuan, and Taiyuan Wang Xiu were all leading younger-generation men of grace and fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng together with Dunqiu Li Ruo, Pengcheng Liu Taizhen, Henan Lu Yanshi, Longxi Xin Deyuan, and Taiyuan Wang Xiu were all leading younger-generation men of grace and fashion.

sentences.zh: 昌衡從父弟思道，魏處士道亮之子，神情俊發，少以才學有盛名。

translations.literal: Changheng's younger cousin from father's line Sidao was son of Wei unreclused Daoliang; his spirit and expression were brilliant, and from youth he had great fame for talent and learning.
translations.idiomatic: Changheng's younger cousin from his father's line Sidao was son of Wei unreclused Daoliang; his spirit and expression were brilliant, and from youth he had great fame for talent and learning.

sentences.zh: 武平末，黃門侍郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: Late in Wuping he was vice director of the yellow gate and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature Hall.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wuping he was vice director of the yellow gate and awaited edicts at the Forest of Literature Hall.

sentences.zh: 思道從父兄正達、正思、正山，魏右光祿大夫道約之子。

translations.literal: Sidao's elder cousins from father's line Zhengda, Zhengsi, and Zhengshan were sons of Wei right director of the shining grandee Daoyue.
translations.idiomatic: Sidao's elder cousins from his father's line Zhengda, Zhengsi, and Zhengshan were sons of Wei right director of the shining grandee Daoyue.

sentences.zh: 正達尚書郎，正思北徐州刺史、太子詹事、儀同三司，正山永昌郡守。

translations.literal: Zhengda was gentleman of the masters of writing; Zhengsi was inspector of Northern Xuzhou, crown-prince grand tutor, equal in insignia to the Three Excellencies; Zhengshan was administrator of Yongchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengda was gentleman of the masters of writing; Zhengsi was inspector of Northern Xuzhou, crown-prince grand tutor, and equal in insignia to the three excellencies; Zhengshan was administrator of Yongchang commandery.

sentences.zh: 兄弟以后舅，武平中並得優贈。

translations.literal: The brothers because they were maternal uncles of the emperor in Wuping all received preferential posthumous enfeoffments.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers, because they were maternal uncles of the emperor, in Wuping all received preferential posthumous enfeoffments.

sentences.zh: 正山子公順，早以文學見知。

translations.literal: Gong Shun, son of Zheng Shan, was early known for his literary learning.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Shun, son of Zheng Shan, won notice early for his literary gifts.

sentences.zh: 武平中符璽郎，待詔文林館。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was seal-letter gentleman and attendant at the Wenslin Hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he served as seal-letter gentleman and as an attendant at the Wenslin Hall.

sentences.zh: 與博陵崔君洽、隴西李師上同志友善，從駕晉陽，寓居僧寺，朝士謂「康寺三少，」為物論推許。

translations.literal: With Cui Junqia of Boling and Li Shishang of Longxi he was united in mind and friendship; following the imperial progress to Jinyang they lodged in a monk's temple. Court men called them "the Three Youngsters of Kang Temple," and public opinion ranked them highly.
translations.idiomatic: He was close in spirit with Cui Junqia of Boling and Li Shishang of Longxi. When the court went to Jinyang they lodged together in a monastery, and colleagues dubbed them "the Three Youngsters of Kang Temple"—a name the age endorsed.

sentences.zh: 正達從父弟熙裕，父道舒。

translations.literal: Zheng Zhengda's younger cousin by the father's line was Xiyu; his father was Daoshu.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Zhengda's younger cousin Xiyu was the son of Daoshu.

sentences.zh: 為長兄道將讓爵，由是熙裕襲固安伯。

translations.literal: Because his elder brother Daojiang yielded the enfeoffment, Xiyu thereby inherited Baron of Gu'an.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Daojiang yielded the title, and Xiyu thereby inherited the barony of Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 虛淡守道，有古人之風，為親表所敬重。

translations.literal: Empty and mild, he kept the Way, had the air of the ancients, and was respected by kin and affines.
translations.idiomatic: Withdrawn and steady, he held to the Way with an antique bearing, and kin and affines held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 潛從祖兄愻之，魏尚書義僖之子。

translations.literal: Lu Qian's elder cousin by the father's line Sunzhi was son of Wei Minister of Works Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian's elder cousin Sunzhi was the son of Wei Minister of Works Yixi.

sentences.zh: 清靖寡欲，卒於司徒記室參軍。

translations.literal: Pure and quiet, few desires; he died as recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: Pure, quiet, and sparing in desire, he ended his days as recorder in the grand tutor's office.

sentences.zh: 崔劼，字彥玄，本清河人。

translations.literal: Cui Jie, styled Yanxuan, was originally a man of Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Jie, styled Yanxuan, came from Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 曾祖曠，南渡河，居青州之東，時宋氏於河南立冀州，置郡縣，卽為東清河郡人。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Kuang crossed south of the Yellow River and settled in eastern Qing province. When the Song house established Ji province south of the Yellow River and set commanderies and counties, he thereby became a man of Eastern Qinghe commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Kuang crossed the Yellow River southward and settled in eastern Qing province. When the Song regime set up Ji province south of the river with its commanderies and counties, the family became men of Eastern Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 南縣分易，更為南平原貝丘人也。

translations.literal: When Nan county was divided and changed, he became moreover a man of Beiqiu in southern Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Nan county was redivided, they were reckoned instead as men of Beiqiu in southern Pingyuan.

sentences.zh: 世為三齊大族。

translations.literal: For generations they were a great clan of the Three Qi.
translations.idiomatic: For generations they ranked among the great clans of the Three Qi.

sentences.zh: 祖靈延，宋長廣太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lingyan was Song governor of Changguang.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lingyan had been Song governor of Changguang.

sentences.zh: 父光，魏太保。

translations.literal: His father Guang was Wei Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guang had been Wei grand guardian.

sentences.zh: 劼少而清虛寡欲，好學有家風。

translations.literal: Jie in youth was pure and empty, few desires, loved learning, and had family style.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jie was spare in wants, loved study, and carried the family's scholarly tone.

sentences.zh: 魏末，自開府行參軍歷尚書儀曹郎、秘書丞，修起居注，中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the end of Wei, from staff gentleman in the opening office he passed through gentleman of ritual observances in the ministry, secretariat director, compiler of the Veritable Records, and secretariat vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wei he rose from staff gentleman in an opening office through ritual observances in the ministry, secretariat director, compiler of the Veritable Records, and secretariat vice-director.

sentences.zh: 興和三年，兼通直散騎常侍，使于梁。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xinghe, concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, envoy to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Xinghe year he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and sent as envoy to Liang.

sentences.zh: 天保初，以議禪代，除給事黃門侍郎，加國子祭酒，直內省，典機密。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao, for discussing the abdication and change of dynasty, he was made gentleman of the yellow gate, added national university libationer, direct in the inner court, managing secrets.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao, for his part in debating the abdication and dynastic change, he was made gentleman of the yellow gate, named national university libationer, and placed in the inner court to handle secrets.

sentences.zh: 清儉勤慎，甚為顯祖所知。

translations.literal: Pure, frugal, diligent, and careful—he was greatly known to Emperor Xianzu.
translations.idiomatic: Frugal, diligent, and careful, he won deep notice from Emperor Xianzu.

sentences.zh: 拜南青州刺史，在任有政績。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Southern Qing province; in office he had administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed governor of Southern Qing, he governed with clear results.

sentences.zh: 皇建中，入為秘書監、齊州大中正，轉鴻臚卿，遷幷省度支尚書，俄授京省，尋轉五兵尚書，監國史，在臺閣之中，見稱簡正。

translations.literal: In Huangjian he entered as director of the secretariat, grand rectifier of Qi province, transferred to director of the Honglu, moved to merged-bureau director of revenue in the masters of writing, soon given capital office, soon transferred to director of the five armies in the masters of writing, supervised the national history; within the terrace pavilions he was called simple and upright.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangjian he entered as secretariat director and grand rectifier of Qi, then director of the Honglu, then merged-bureau director of revenue, soon given a capital post, then director of the five armies while supervising the national history. Within the terrace offices he was praised as plain and correct.

sentences.zh: 世祖之將禪後主，先以問劼，劼諫以為不可，由是忤意，出為南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu was about to abdicate to the Later Sovereign, he first asked Jie; Jie remonstrated that it could not be done; thereby going against his intent, he was sent out as governor of Southern Yan.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu prepared to yield the throne to the Later Sovereign, he first consulted Jie. Jie urged that it must not be done; the advice crossed his will, and Jie was sent out as governor of Southern Yan.

sentences.zh: 代還，重為度支尚書、儀同三司，食文登縣幹。

translations.literal: On returning from replacement, he was again made director of revenue and peer of the three ranks, with fief income from Wen commandery dry.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from the province, he was again director of revenue and peer of the three ranks, drawing salary from Wen commandery dry.

sentences.zh: 尋除中書令，加開府，待詔文林館，監撰新書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made secretariat director, added an open office, attendant at the Wenslin Hall, supervising compilation of the new book.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was secretariat director with an open office, attended at the Wenslin Hall, and supervised compilation of the new book.

sentences.zh: 遇病卒，時年六十六。

translations.literal: He met illness and died, aged sixty-six at the time.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 贈齊州刺史、尚書右僕射，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given governor of Qi, right vice director of the masters of writing, posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Qi and right vice director of the masters of writing, with the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 初，和士開擅朝，曲求物譽，諸公因此頗為子弟幹祿，世門之胄，多處京官，而劼二子拱、捴並為外任。

translations.literal: At first He Shikai monopolized the court and curried reputation by devious means; the various dukes therefore quite sought offices and stipends for their sons. Sons of eminent gates mostly held capital offices, while Jie's two sons Gong and Zong both held outer appointments.
translations.idiomatic: At first He Shikai dominated the court and courted praise by crooked means, so great families pressed for offices and stipends for their sons. Scions of eminent houses mostly held capital posts, but Jie's sons Gong and Zong both served in the provinces.

sentences.zh: 弟廓之從容謂劼曰：「拱、捴幸得不凡，何為不在省府之中、清華之所，而並出外藩，有損家代。

translations.literal: His younger brother Kuozhi said at ease to Jie: "Gong and Zong are lucky to be no ordinary men—why are they not in the provincial offices and pure eminent posts, but both go to outer provinces, harming the family line for generations?"
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Kuozhi said privately to Jie, "Gong and Zong are plainly gifted—why keep them out of the capital's pure offices and send them both to the provinces, to the family's hurt for generations?"

sentences.zh: 」劼曰：「立身以來，恥以一言自達，今若進兒，與身何異。

translations.literal: Jie said: "Since establishing myself I have been ashamed to advance by a single word; now if I promote my sons, how does that differ from me?"
translations.idiomatic: Jie said, "All my life I have been ashamed to advance by a single word of favor. If I now push my sons forward, how is that different from pushing myself?"

sentences.zh: 」卒無所求。

translations.literal: In the end he sought nothing.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he asked for nothing.

sentences.zh: 聞者莫不嘆服。

translations.literal: Those who heard all sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: All who heard it sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 拱，天統中任城王湝丞相諮議參軍、管記室。

translations.literal: Gong, in Tiantong, served Prince of Rencheng Gao Chun as staff deliberator and managed the records office.
translations.idiomatic: Gong, in Tiantong, was staff deliberator to Prince of Rencheng Gao Chun and ran his records office.

sentences.zh: 撝，揚州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Hui was Yangzhou recorder.
translations.idiomatic: Hui served as Yangzhou recorder.

sentences.zh: 廓之沉隱有識量，以學業見稱。

translations.literal: Kuozhi was deep and retiring, with discernment, and was famed for scholarship.
translations.idiomatic: Kuozhi was reserved and discerning, famed for scholarship.

sentences.zh: 自臨水令為瑯邪王儼大司馬西閤祭酒，遷領軍功曹參軍。

translations.literal: From magistrate of Linshui he became western-pavilion libationer in Prince of Langye Yan's grand marshal establishment, then moved to merit staff in the guard corps.
translations.idiomatic: From magistrate of Linshui he rose to western-pavilion libationer under Prince of Langye Yan's grand marshal, then to merit staff in the guard corps.

sentences.zh: 武平中卒。

translations.literal: He died in Wuping.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Wuping.

sentences.zh: 盧叔武，范陽涿人，青州刺史文偉從子也。

translations.literal: Lu Shuqi, a man of Zhuo in Fanyang, was nephew of Qing province governor Wenwei.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Shuqi came from Zhuo in Fanyang and was nephew to Qing province governor Wenwei.

sentences.zh: 父光宗，有志尚。

translations.literal: His father Guangzong had will and aspiration.
translations.idiomatic: His father Guangzong had force of character.

sentences.zh: 叔武兩兄觀、仲宣並以文章顯於洛下。

translations.literal: Shuqi's two elder brothers Guan and Zhongxuan both were famed in Luoyang for their writing.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqi's elder brothers Guan and Zhongxuan had both won fame in Luoyang for their writing.

sentences.zh: 叔武少機悟，豪率輕俠，好奇策，慕諸葛亮之為人。

translations.literal: Shuqi in youth was quick-witted, bold and free, light and chivalric, loved clever stratagems, and admired Zhuge Liang as a man.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Shuqi was quick-witted, bold and open-handed, fond of clever plans, and took Zhuge Liang for his model.

sentences.zh: 為賀拔勝荊州開府長史。

translations.literal: Heluo Sheng appointed him long staff in the Jing province opening office.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Sheng made him long staff in the Jing province opening office.

sentences.zh: 勝不用其計，棄城奔梁。

translations.literal: Sheng did not use his plans; he abandoned the city and fled to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng ignored his plans, abandoned the city, and fled to Liang.

sentences.zh: 叔武歸本縣，築室臨陂，優遊自適。

translations.literal: Shuqi returned to his home county, built a chamber by the pond, and dwelt at ease in leisure.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqi went home to his county, built a house by the waters, and lived at ease.

sentences.zh: 世宗降辟書，辭疾不到。

translations.literal: Emperor Shizong sent a summons scroll; he pleaded illness and did not come.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizong sent a summons; he pleaded illness and stayed away.

sentences.zh: 天保初復徵，不得已，布裘乘露車至鄴。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianbao he was summoned again; unable to refuse, in a cloth fur robe he rode an open cart to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Tianbao he was summoned again. Unable to refuse, he came to Ye in a cloth cloak aboard an open cart.

sentences.zh: 楊愔往候之，以為司徒諮議，稱疾不受。

translations.literal: Yang Yin went to visit him, intending to make him staff deliberator for the Secretariat Director; he claimed illness and would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Yin called on him to make him staff deliberator to the director of the secretariat, but he pleaded illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 肅宗卽位，召為太子中庶子，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When Prince Suzong took the throne he was summoned as heir apparent vice-director, added silver-blue-gleaming grand master.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Suzong took the throne he was summoned as heir-apparent vice-director and given the silver-blue-gleaming grand master cap.

sentences.zh: 問以世事，叔武勸討關西，畫地陳兵勢曰：「人衆敵者當任智謀，鈞者當任勢力，故強者所以制弱，富者所以兼貧。

translations.literal: Asked about current affairs, Shuqi urged campaigning against the west, drew on the ground and stated troop dispositions, saying: "When the many face the foe, one should employ strategy; when equal, one should employ force—thus the strong can control the weak, the rich can annex the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Asked about affairs of the day, Shuqi urged war in the west, sketched dispositions on the ground, and said, "When numbers match the enemy, use stratagem; when forces are even, use power—so the strong rule the weak and the rich absorb the poor.

sentences.zh: 今大齊之比關西，強弱不同，貧富有異，而戎馬不息，未能吞並，此失於不用強富也。

translations.literal: Now great Qi compared to the west is not the same in strong and weak, poor and rich, yet war-horses do not rest and still cannot swallow and merge them—this is the fault of not using strength and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: Great Qi and the west are unequal in strength and wealth, yet our horses never rest and we still cannot swallow them—because we refuse to use our strength and wealth.

sentences.zh: 輕兵野戰，勝負難必，是胡騎之法，非深謀遠算萬全之術也。

translations.literal: Light troops in field battle—victory and defeat are hard to fix; that is barbarian-cavalry method, not deep planning and far calculation, the ten-thousandfold-safe art.
translations.idiomatic: Light forces in open battle make victory uncertain—that is nomad cavalry's way, not the long-calculated art that secures all.

sentences.zh: 宜立重鎮於平陽，與彼蒲州相對，深溝高壘，運糧積甲，築城戍以屬之。

translations.literal: One should establish a heavy garrison at Pingyang, facing their Pu province across, with deep moats and high ramparts, transport grain and store armor, and build fortified cities linked to it.
translations.idiomatic: We should plant a strong garrison at Pingyang opposite their Pu province—deep moats, high walls, grain convoys, stored armor, and a chain of walled posts.

sentences.zh: 彼若閉關不出，則取其黃河以東，長安窮蹙，自然困死。

translations.literal: If they close the passes and do not come out, then take their land east of the Yellow River; Chang'an in desperate straits will naturally starve to death.
translations.idiomatic: If they shut the passes and hold inside, we take everything east of the Yellow River; Chang'an, cut off, will waste away on its own.

sentences.zh: 如彼出兵，非十萬以上，不為我敵，所供糧食，皆出關內。

translations.literal: If they send troops out, unless more than a hundred thousand they are not our match; the grain they supply all comes from within the passes.
translations.idiomatic: If they march out, they need more than a hundred thousand men to match us, and every bushel they eat must come from inside the passes.

sentences.zh: 我兵士相代，年別一番，谷食豐饒，運送不絕。

translations.literal: Our soldiers rotate in shifts, each year one rotation; grain food is abundant and transport unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Our troops would rotate yearly; our granaries are full and convoys steady.

sentences.zh: 彼來求戰，我不應之，彼若退軍，卽乘其弊。

translations.literal: If they come to seek battle we do not respond; if they withdraw their army, then seize their weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Let them offer battle and we do not answer; let them retreat and we strike the opening.

sentences.zh: 自長安以西，民疏城遠，敵兵來往，實有艱難，與我相持，農作且廢，不過三年，彼自破矣。

translations.literal: From Chang'an westward, people are sparse and cities far—enemy troops coming and going truly have hardship; holding against us, farming moreover is abandoned; within no more than three years they will break themselves.
translations.idiomatic: West of Chang'an the land is thin of people and far between towns—every march costs them dearly. Locked with us, they cannot farm; in three years they will break themselves.

sentences.zh: 」帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the plan to heart.

sentences.zh: 又願自居平陽，成此謀略。

translations.literal: He also wished to place himself at Pingyang and carry out this strategy.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to hold Pingyang himself and carry the plan through.

sentences.zh: 上令元文遙與叔武參謀，撰《平西策》一卷。

translations.literal: The sovereign ordered Yuan Wenyao and Shuqi together to plan and compile one scroll of the Pacifying-the-West Stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: The throne ordered Yuan Wenyao and Shuqi to draft together a scroll called the Pacifying-the-West Stratagem.

sentences.zh: 未幾帝崩，事遂寢。

translations.literal: Before long the emperor died and the matter then slept.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the emperor died and the scheme lapsed.

sentences.zh: 世祖踐阼，拜儀同三司、都官尚書，出為合州刺史。

translations.literal: When Emperor Shizu trod the throne, he was made peer of the three ranks and director of punishments in the masters of writing, then sent out as governor of He province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizu ascended, he was made peer of the three ranks and director of punishments, then sent out as governor of He.

sentences.zh: 武平中，遷太子詹事、右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was moved to heir apparent tutor and right grand master with gleaming cap.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was moved to heir-apparent tutor and right grand master with gleaming cap.

sentences.zh: 叔武在鄉時有粟千石，每至春夏，鄉人無食者令自載取，至秋，任其償，都不計校。

translations.literal: When Shuqi was in the village he had a thousand dan of grain; each spring and summer when villagers had no food he had them load and take for themselves; by autumn he left repayment to them and entirely did not calculate accounts.
translations.idiomatic: At home Shuqi kept a thousand dan of grain. Each spring and summer, when neighbors lacked food, he let them haul what they needed; come autumn he left repayment to their conscience and kept no accounts.

sentences.zh: 然而歲歲常得倍餘。

translations.literal: Yet year after year he always gained more than double.
translations.idiomatic: Year after year he still ended with more than twice as much.

sentences.zh: 旣在朝通貴，自以年老，兒子又多，遂營一大屋，曰：「歌於斯，哭於斯。

translations.literal: Once in court eminent and honored, seeing himself old with many sons, he therefore built one great house, saying: "Here we sing; here we weep.
translations.idiomatic: Once eminent at court, old and with many sons, he built one great house and said, "Here we shall sing; here we shall mourn.

sentences.zh: 」魏收曾來詣之，訪以洛京舊事，不待食而起，云：「難為子費。

translations.literal: " Wei Shou once came to call on him and inquired about old matters of the Luoyang capital; before food arrived he rose, saying, "Hard to burden the host's expense.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Shou once called to ask about old Luoyang. Before food came he rose and said, "I hate to burden your table.

sentences.zh: 」叔武留之，良久食至，但有粟餐菜，木碗盛之，片脯而已。

translations.literal: " Shuqi detained him; after a long while food came—only millet meal and vegetables in wooden bowls, with a slice of dried meat only.
translations.idiomatic: " Shuqi kept him. Long after, the meal came—millet and greens in wooden bowls and a single slice of dried meat.

sentences.zh: 所將仆從，亦盡設食，一與此同。

translations.literal: The attendants he brought were also all set food, each the same as this.
translations.idiomatic: The servants he had brought were fed the same.

sentences.zh: 齊滅，歸范陽，遭亂城陷，叔武與族弟士遂皆以寒餧至斃。

translations.literal: When Qi perished he returned to Fanyang; he met turmoil and the city fell; Shuqi and clansman Shisui both died from cold porridge to the end.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he returned to Fanyang. In the turmoil the city was taken; Shuqi and his clansman Shisui both starved on cold gruel.

sentences.zh: 周將宇文神舉以其有名德，收而葬之。

translations.literal: Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, because of his fame and virtue, gathered and buried them.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou general Yuwen Shenju, honoring their name and conduct, gathered and buried them.

sentences.zh: 叔武族孫臣客，父子規，魏尚書郎、林慮郡守。

translations.literal: Shuqi's clansman by the younger generation Chenke—his father Gui was Wei gentleman of the masters of writing and governor of Linlu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Shuqi's younger clansman Chenke was the son of Gui, who had been Wei gentleman of the masters of writing and governor of Linlu.

sentences.zh: 臣客風儀甚美，少有志尚，雅有法度，好道家之言。

translations.literal: Chenke's bearing was very fine; in youth he had will and aspiration, was refined in law and measure, and loved Daoist discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Chenke's bearing was striking; young, he had purpose, kept precise habits, and loved Daoist teaching.

sentences.zh: 其姊為任城王妃，天保末，任城王致之於朝廷，由是擢拜太子舍人。

translations.literal: His elder sister was consort of Prince of Rencheng; at the end of Tianbao Prince of Rencheng brought him to court, thereby promoted to heir apparent attender.
translations.idiomatic: His elder sister was consort to Prince of Rencheng. At the end of Tianbao the prince brought him to court and had him made heir-apparent attender.

sentences.zh: 遷司徒記室，請歸侍祖母李。

translations.literal: He was moved to recorder in the Secretariat Director and asked leave to return and serve his grandmother Li.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to recorder under the secretariat director, he asked leave to go home and care for his grandmother Li.

sentences.zh: 李強之令仕，不得已而順命，除太子舍人、太子中庶子。

translations.literal: Li strongly ordered him to take office; unable to refuse, he followed the order—made heir apparent attender and heir apparent vice-director.
translations.idiomatic: Li pressed him to serve; he could not refuse and accepted—again heir-apparent attender and then vice-director.

sentences.zh: 武平中，兼散騎常侍，聘陳，還，卒於路。

translations.literal: In Wuping he was concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, envoy to Chen; on return he died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: In Wuping he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and envoy to Chen; he died on the road home.

sentences.zh: 贈鄭州刺史、鴻臚卿。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was given governor of Zheng and director of the Honglu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor of Zheng and director of the Honglu.

sentences.zh: 陽休之，字子烈，右北平無終人也。

translations.literal: Yang Xiuzhi, styled Zilie, was a man of Wuzhong in right Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuzhi, styled Zilie, came from Wuzhong in Youbeiping.

sentences.zh: 父固，魏洛陽令，贈太常少卿。

translations.literal: His father Gu was Wei magistrate of Luoyang, posthumously given vice director of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu had been Wei magistrate of Luoyang and was posthumously made vice director of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 休之儁爽有風概，少勤學，愛文藻，弱冠擅聲，為後來之秀，幽州刺史常景、王延年並召為州主簿。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi was handsome and spirited, with bearing; in youth he was diligent in study, loved literary ornament, and at weak cap held the voice—the outstanding talent of his generation. You province governors Chang Jing and Wang Yannian both summoned him as provincial chief clerk.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was sharp and high-spirited. He studied hard in youth, loved letters, and at twenty already led his generation in renown. You province governors Chang Jing and Wang Yannian both made him provincial chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 魏孝昌中，杜洛周破薊城，休之與宗室及鄉人數千家南奔章武，轉至青州。

translations.literal: In Xiaochang of Wei, Du Luozhou broke Ji city; Xiuzhi with the imperial clan and several thousand fellow townsmen fled south to Zhangwu, then on to Qing province.
translations.idiomatic: In Wei Xiaochang, Du Luozhou took Ji. Xiuzhi fled south with kinsmen and several thousand townsfolk to Zhangwu, then to Qing province.

sentences.zh: 是時葛榮寇亂，河北流民多湊青部。

translations.literal: At that time Ge Rong's bandit turmoil spread; refugees from Hebei mostly crowded into Qing.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Rong's rebellion was raging, and Hebei refugees poured into Qing.

sentences.zh: 休之知將有變，乃請其族叔伯彥等曰：「客主勢異，競相淩侮，禍難將作。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi knew change was coming and therefore asked his clan uncle Boyan and others, saying: "Guest and host differ in strength; they vie to insult one another—calamity is about to arise.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi saw trouble coming and told his uncle Boyan and the rest, "Hosts and guests are unequal in power; they will bully one another until disaster strikes.

sentences.zh: 如鄙情所見，宜潛歸京師避之。

translations.literal: As my humble view sees it, we ought secretly to return to the capital and avoid it.
translations.idiomatic: As I see it, we should slip back to the capital while we can.

sentences.zh: 」諸人多不能從。

translations.literal: " Most could not follow.
translations.idiomatic: " Most would not go.

sentences.zh: 休之垂涕別去。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi parted with tears and left.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi wept and took his leave.

sentences.zh: 俄而邢杲作亂，伯彥等咸為土民所殺，一時遇害，諸陽死者數十人，唯休之兄弟獲免。

translations.literal: Soon Xing Shuo rose in rebellion; Boyan and the rest were all killed by local people, slain at one stroke—of the Yang clan several tens died, and only Xiuzhi and his brothers escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Xing Shuo rebelled. Boyan and the others were killed by locals in a single sweep; dozens of the Yang clan died, and only Xiuzhi and his brothers escaped.

sentences.zh: 莊帝立，解褐員外散騎侍郎，尋以本官領御史，遷給事中、太尉記室參軍，加輕車將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, he doffed commoner's garb as irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, soon in that office led the censorate, moved to attendant within the palace and recorder in the Grand Tutor's establishment, added light-chariot general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang took the throne, Xiuzhi entered service as irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, soon led the censorate in that rank, then became palace attendant and recorder to the grand tutor, with the added title light-chariot general.

sentences.zh: 李神俊監起居注，啟休之與河東裴伯茂、范陽盧元明、河間邢子明等俱入撰次。

translations.literal: Li Shenjun supervised the Veritable Records and memorialized that Xiuzhi, with Hedong Pei Bomo, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Hejian Xing Ziming, and others should all enter to compile in order.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenjun oversaw the Veritable Records and had Xiuzhi join Hedong Pei Bomo, Fanyang Lu Yuanming, Hejian Xing Ziming, and others in the compilation.

sentences.zh: 永安末，洛州刺史李海啟除冠軍長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Yong'an he was, on memorial of Luozhou governor Li Hai, made champion long staff.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Yong'an, on Luozhou governor Li Hai's memorial, he was made champion long staff.

sentences.zh: 普泰中，兼通直散騎侍郎，加鎮遠將軍，尋為太保長孫稚府屬。

translations.literal: In Putai he was concurrently irregular-attendant cavalier attendant, added general who subdues the far, soon staff in Grand Guardian Sun Sui's establishment.
translations.idiomatic: In Putai he was also irregular-attendant cavalier attendant and general who subdues the far, then joined Grand Guardian Sun Sui's staff.

sentences.zh: 尋勑與魏收、李同軌等修國史。

translations.literal: Soon an edict ordered him with Wei Shou, Li Tonggui, and others to revise the national history.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict set him with Wei Shou, Li Tonggui, and others to revise the national history.

sentences.zh: 太昌初，除尚書祠部郎中，尋進征虜將軍、中散大夫。

translations.literal: Early in Taichang he was made gentleman of the ancestral temple section in the ministry, soon advanced to general who campaigns against the barbarians and grand master who scatters the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Taichang he was made gentleman of the ancestral-temple section, then advanced to general who campaigns against the barbarians and grand master who scatters the masses.

sentences.zh: 賀拔勝出為荊州刺史，啟補驃騎長史。

translations.literal: Heluo Sheng went out as governor of Jing province and memorialized to fill the post of swift-cavalry long staff.
translations.idiomatic: Heluo Sheng went out as Jing governor and had him appointed swift-cavalry long staff.

sentences.zh: 勝為行臺，又請為右丞。

translations.literal: Sheng held a mobile headquarters and again asked for him as right vice director.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng held a field headquarters he asked again for him as right vice director.

sentences.zh: 勝經略樊、沔，又請為南道軍司。

translations.literal: Sheng managed Fan and Mian, and again asked for him as southern-route army marshal.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning on the Fan and Mian front, Sheng again asked for him as southern-route army marshal.

sentences.zh: 俄而魏武帝入關，勝令休之奉表詣長安參謁。

translations.literal: Soon Emperor Wu of Wei entered the passes; Sheng ordered Xiuzhi to present a memorial and go to Chang'an to attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Emperor Wu of Wei entered the passes. Sheng ordered Xiuzhi to carry a memorial to Chang'an for audience.

sentences.zh: 時高祖亦啟除休之太常少卿。

translations.literal: At that time the High Ancestor also memorialized to appoint Xiuzhi vice director of splendid happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time the High Ancestor memorialized to make Xiuzhi vice director of splendid happiness.

sentences.zh: 尋屬勝南奔，仍隨至建業。

translations.literal: Soon, following Sheng's flight south, he still followed to Jianye.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, when Sheng fled south, Xiuzhi followed him to Jianye.

sentences.zh: 休之聞高祖推奉靜帝，乃白勝啟梁武求還，以天平二年達鄴，仍奉高祖命赴晉陽。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi heard the High Ancestor was promoting and supporting Emperor Jing; he therefore told Sheng to memorialize Liang Wu to request return. In the second year of Tianping he reached Ye and still followed the High Ancestor's order to go to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the High Ancestor was raising and supporting Emperor Jing, Xiuzhi urged Sheng to ask Liang Wu for leave to return. In the second Tianping year he reached Ye, then went to Jinyang on the High Ancestor's command.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，授世宗開府主簿。

translations.literal: That winter he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Sovereign's Office under the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he was appointed chief secretary in the Heir Apparent's sovereign office.

sentences.zh: 明年春，世宗為大行臺，復引為行臺郎中。

translations.literal: The next spring, when the Heir Apparent became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, he was again brought in as Bureau Director of the Commissionerate.
translations.idiomatic: The next spring, when the Heir Apparent became Grand Commissioner-in-Chief, Yang was again made a bureau director of the commissionerate.

sentences.zh: 四年，高祖幸汾陽之天池，於池邊得一石，上有隱起，其文曰「六王三川」。

translations.literal: In year four, Emperor Gaozu visited the Heavenly Pool at Fenyang; beside the pool he found a stone with raised characters reading "Six, King, Three Rivers."
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, Emperor Gaozu visited the Heavenly Pool at Fenyang and found beside it a stone with raised characters: "Six, King, Three Rivers."

sentences.zh: 高祖獨於帳中問之，此文字何義，對曰：「六者是大王之字，王者當王有天下，此乃大王符瑞受命之徵。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu asked him alone in the tent what these characters meant; he replied: "Six is the character for 'great king'; a king ought to rule all under Heaven—this is a sign of your destined mandate and token of receiving the mandate."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu asked him alone in the tent what the inscription meant. Yang answered: "Six is the character for 'great king'; a king ought to rule all under Heaven—this is the omen of your destined mandate."

sentences.zh: 旣於天池得此石，可謂天意命王也，吉不可言。

translations.literal: Now that this stone was obtained at the Heavenly Pool, it may be called Heaven's intent appointing you king—the auspice is beyond words.
translations.idiomatic: Now that this stone came from the Heavenly Pool, it is Heaven appointing you king—the auspice is beyond words.

sentences.zh: 」高祖又問三川何義，休之曰：「河、洛、伊為三川，亦雲涇、渭、洛為三川。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu again asked what "Three Rivers" meant; Xiuzhi said: "The Yellow, Luo, and Yi are called the Three Rivers; some also say the Jing, Wei, and Luo."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked what "Three Rivers" meant. Xiuzhi said: "The Yellow, Luo, and Yi are one Three Rivers; some also name the Jing, Wei, and Luo."

sentences.zh: 河、洛、伊，洛陽也；

translations.literal: The Yellow, Luo, and Yi—that is Luoyang;
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow, Luo, and Yi—that is Luoyang;

sentences.zh: 涇、渭、洛，今雍州也。

translations.literal: the Jing, Wei, and Luo—that is present-day Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: the Jing, Wei, and Luo—that is present-day Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 大王若受天命，終應統有關右。

translations.literal: If the Great King receives Heaven's mandate, in the end he ought to rule the whole Guanzhong region."
translations.idiomatic: "If the Great King receives Heaven's mandate, in the end he will hold all of Guanzhong."

sentences.zh: 」高祖曰：「世人無事常道我欲反，今聞此，更致紛紜，慎莫妄言也。」

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu said: "When people have nothing better to do they constantly say I intend rebellion; now that they hear this, it will stir more commotion—be careful not to speak rashly."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu said: "Idle tongues are forever saying I mean to rebel; if word of this spreads, the uproar will only grow—do not speak of it lightly."

sentences.zh: 元象初，錄荊州軍功，封新泰縣開國伯，食邑六百戶，除平東將軍、太中大夫、尚書左民郎中。

translations.literal: At the start of Yuanxiang, his military merit at Jing Province was recorded; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai County with state-founder rank, fief of six hundred households, and appointed General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Bureau Director of the Left Department of the People in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Yuanxiang his Jing Province service was entered in the merit rolls; he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xintai with a fief of six hundred households and made General Who Pacifies the East, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and bureau director of the left people's section.

sentences.zh: 興和二年，兼通直散騎常侍，副清河崔長謙使於梁。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xinghe he was concurrently Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadency and served as deputy to Cui Changqian of Qinghe on a mission to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xinghe he was made Regular Attendant of the Palace Cadency and went to Liang as deputy to Cui Changqian of Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 武定二年，除中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wuding he was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Wuding he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時有人士戲嘲休之云：「有觸藩之羝羊，乘連錢之聰馬，從晉陽而向鄴，懷屬書而盈把。

translations.literal: At the time some wits mocked Xiuzhi, saying: "A ram that has touched the hedge-fence, riding a spirited horse with linked-coin markings, from Jinyang toward Ye, clutching a dossier of names till his hands are full."
translations.idiomatic: Some wits then mocked Xiuzhi in verse: "A ram that has brushed the fence, on a spirited horse marked like linked coins, from Jinyang to Ye, with a roster of names clutched till his hands overflow."

sentences.zh: 」尚書左丞盧斐以其文書請謁，啟高祖禁止，會赦不治。

translations.literal: Left Assistant Director of the Ministry Lu Fei submitted his document asking audience; he reported to Emperor Gaozu, who forbade it; an amnesty intervened and he was not punished.
translations.idiomatic: Left assistant director Lu Fei used the lampoon to request an audience; he reported it to Emperor Gaozu, who forbade further action; an amnesty followed and no punishment was imposed.

sentences.zh: 五年，兼尚食典禦。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was concurrently Chief Steward of Imperial Viands.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was concurrently chief steward of imperial viands.

sentences.zh: 七年，除太子中庶子，遷給事黃門侍郎，進號中軍將軍、幽州大中正。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Household Supervisor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Attendant Cavalier of the Yellow Gate, and advanced in rank to General of the Central Army and Chief Rectifier of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made household supervisor of the Heir Apparent, then promoted to Attendant Cavalier of the Yellow Gate and advanced to General of the Central Army and chief rectifier of You Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼侍中，持節奉璽書詣幷州，敦喻顯祖為相國、齊王。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently Palace Attendant, bearing credentials and carrying the imperial seal-letter to Bingzhou to urge Xianzu to accept the titles of Chancellor of State and Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was concurrently palace attendant, bore credentials, and carried the imperial seal-letter to Bingzhou to urge Xianzu to accept the titles Chancellor of State and Prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 是時，顯祖將受魏禪，發晉陽，至平陽郡，為人心未一，且還幷州，恐漏泄，仍斷行人。

translations.literal: At that time Xianzu was about to receive the Wei abdication; he set out from Jinyang and reached Pingyang commandery; because hearts were not yet united he returned for the time being to Bingzhou; fearing leaks, he cut off travel along the roads.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzu was then preparing to receive the Wei abdication; he left Jinyang and reached Pingyang, but because hearts were not yet one he turned back to Bingzhou for the time being; fearing a leak, he cut off traffic on the roads.

sentences.zh: 休之性疏放，使還，遂說其事，鄴中悉知。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi by nature was careless and loose-tongued; when he returned from his mission he spoke of the affair, and everyone in Ye knew.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi was by nature careless and loose-tongued; on his return he spoke of the matter, and all Ye knew.

sentences.zh: 於後高德政以聞，顯祖忿之而未發。

translations.literal: Later Gao Dezheng reported it; Xianzu was angry but did not yet act.
translations.idiomatic: Later Gao Dezheng reported it; Xianzu was angry but held his hand.

sentences.zh: 齊受禪，除散騎常侍，修起居注。

translations.literal: When Qi received the abdication he was appointed Regular Companion of the Fast Cavalry and compiled the Daily Records.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi received the abdication he was made Regular Companion of the Fast Cavalry and put in charge of the Daily Records.

sentences.zh: 頃之，坐詔書脫誤，左遷驍騎將軍，積前事也。

translations.literal: Before long, for errors in omission in an edict, he was demoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry—the accumulated weight of earlier matters.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, for omissions in an edict, he was demoted to General of the Valiant Cavalry—the accumulated weight of earlier offenses.

sentences.zh: 尋以禪讓之際，參定禮儀，別封始平縣開國男，以本官兼領軍司馬。

translations.literal: Soon, at the time of the abdication rites, he took part in fixing the ritual protocol; separately enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping County with state-founder rank, he held his former post while concurrently serving as army marshal of the Guards.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, during the abdication rites, he helped fix the ritual protocol; he was separately enfeoffed as Baron of Shiping and, retaining his post, concurrently served as army marshal of the Guards.

sentences.zh: 後除都水使者，歷司徒掾、中書侍郎，尋除中山太守。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Commissioner of Aqueducts, passed through as staff officer of the Minister of Education and vice director of the Secretariat, and soon was made Administrator of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made commissioner of aqueducts, served as staff officer to the Minister of Education and secretariat vice director, and soon became administrator of Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 顯祖崩，徵休之至晉陽，經紀喪禮。

translations.literal: When Xianzu died, Xiuzhi was summoned to Jinyang to manage the mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Xianzu died, Xiuzhi was summoned to Jinyang to oversee the mourning rites.

sentences.zh: 乾明元年，兼侍中，巡省京邑。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ganming he was concurrently Palace Attendant and inspected the capital district.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Ganming he was concurrently palace attendant and toured the capital district on inspection.

sentences.zh: 仍拜大鴻臚卿，領中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Grand Master for the Glorious Ceremonial, while retaining the vice-directorship of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Master for the Glorious Ceremonial while retaining his secretariat vice-directorship.

sentences.zh: 皇建初，以本官兼度支尚書，加驃騎大將軍，領幽州大中正。

translations.literal: At the start of Huangjian he held his former post while concurrently serving as Minister of Revenue, was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as Chief Rectifier of You Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Huangjian he kept his post while concurrently serving as Minister of Revenue, was advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and continued as chief rectifier of You Province.

sentences.zh: 肅宗留心政道，每訪休之治術。

translations.literal: Emperor Suzong minded the arts of government and often consulted Xiuzhi on methods of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong attended closely to governance and often asked Xiuzhi for counsel on how to rule.

sentences.zh: 休之答以明賞罰、慎官方、禁淫侈、恤民患為政治之先。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi answered that clear rewards and punishments, careful management of officials, prohibition of excess and extravagance, and compassion for the people's hardships must come first in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi answered that governance must begin with clear rewards and punishments, careful control of officials, curbing excess and extravagance, and relieving the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 帝深納之。

translations.literal: The emperor took this deeply to heart.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his advice deeply to heart.

sentences.zh: 大寧中，除都官尚書，轉七兵、祠部。

translations.literal: During the Daning era he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the ministries of military affairs and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During Daning he was appointed Minister of Justice, then transferred to the military and sacrifices ministries.

sentences.zh: 河清三年，出為西兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Heqing he went out as Governor of Western Yan Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Heqing he went out as governor of Western Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 天統初，徵為光祿卿，監國史。

translations.literal: At the start of Tiantong he was recalled as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and oversaw the national history.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tiantong he was recalled as Chamberlain for the Imperial Clan and put in charge of the national history.

sentences.zh: 休之在中山及治西兗，俱有惠政，為吏民所懷。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi in Zhongshan and when governing Western Yan alike had benevolent policies and was cherished by officials and commoners.
translations.idiomatic: Whether in Zhongshan or governing Western Yan, Xiuzhi pursued benevolent policies and won the affection of officials and commoners alike.

sentences.zh: 去官之後，百姓樹碑頌德。

translations.literal: After he left office the people erected steles praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: After he left office the people raised steles in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 尋除吏部尚書，食陽武縣幹，除儀同三司，又加開府。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of the Civil Service, drew income from the Yangwu county fief-stipend, was made Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and further given the sovereign's office privilege.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of the Civil Service, drew income from the Yangwu county stipend, was given Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and further granted a sovereign's office.

sentences.zh: 休之多識故事，諳悉氏族，凡所選用，莫不才地俱允。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi knew many precedents and was thoroughly versed in clans; every appointment he made was apt both in talent and in social standing.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi knew precedent inside out and understood clans thoroughly; every man he appointed was fit both in talent and in pedigree.

sentences.zh: 加金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.
translations.idiomatic: He was advanced to Grand Master with Golden Girdle and Purple Purse.

sentences.zh: 武平元年，除中書監，尋以本官兼尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wuping he was appointed Secretariat Director; soon, retaining that post, he was concurrently Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Wuping he was made secretariat director; soon, retaining that post, he was concurrently right vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 二年，加左光祿大夫，兼中書監。
