translations.literal: In the second year he was advanced to Left Grand Master for the Glorious, while concurrently Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was advanced to Left Grand Master for the Glorious while remaining secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 三年，加特進。

translations.literal: In the third year he was given the Extraordinary Advancement.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was given the rank of Extraordinary Advancement.

sentences.zh: 五年，正中書監，餘並如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was made regular Secretariat Director; the rest of his posts remained unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was made regular secretariat director; his other posts stayed as they were.

sentences.zh: 尋以年老致仕，抗表辭位，帝優答不許。

translations.literal: Soon, citing age, he sought retirement; he submitted a memorial refusing office; the emperor answered graciously but would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, citing age, he sought retirement and submitted a memorial resigning his posts; the emperor answered graciously but would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 六年，除正尚書右僕射。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made regular Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made regular right vice director of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 未幾，又領中書監。

translations.literal: Before long he again headed the Secretariat as Director.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he again headed the Secretariat as director.

sentences.zh: 休之本懷平坦，為士友所稱。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi by nature was even-tempered and was praised by scholar-friends.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Xiuzhi was even-tempered, and scholar-friends spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 晚節說祖珽撰《御覽》，書成，加特進，及珽被黜，便布言於朝廷，云先有嫌隙。

translations.literal: In his later years he urged Zu Ting to compile the Imperial Overview; when the book was finished he was given Extraordinary Advancement; when Ting was dismissed he spread word through court that there had been old animosity between them.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he urged Zu Ting to compile the Imperial Overview; when the book was finished he was given Extraordinary Advancement; when Ting was dismissed he spread word at court that they had long been at odds.

sentences.zh: 及鄧長颙、顏之推奏立文林館，之推本意不欲令耆舊貴人居之，休之便相附會，與少年朝請、參軍之徒同入待詔。

translations.literal: When Deng Changxuan and Yan Zhitui memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall, Zhitui had not intended that elderly eminent men hold posts there; Xiuzhi went along with it and entered together with young court gentlemen and staff officers as editors awaiting edicts.
translations.idiomatic: When Deng Changxuan and Yan Zhitui memorialized to establish the Forest of Literature Hall, Zhitui had not wanted elderly eminent men inside; Xiuzhi went along anyway and entered with young court gentlemen and staff officers as editors awaiting edicts.

sentences.zh: 又魏收監史之日，立《高祖本紀》，取平四胡之歲為齊元。

translations.literal: Again, when Wei Shou oversaw the history, he drew up the Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu and took the year of pacifying the Four Barbarians as the founding year of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Again, while Wei Shou oversaw the history, he drafted the Basic Annals of Emperor Gaozu and took the year of pacifying the Four Barbarians as Qi's founding year.

sentences.zh: 收在齊州，恐史官改奪其意，上表論之。

translations.literal: Shou was in Qi Province and feared the historiographers would alter his intent; he submitted a memorial arguing the point.
translations.idiomatic: Shou was then in Qi Province and feared the historiographers would overturn his intent; he submitted a memorial arguing his case.

sentences.zh: 武平中，收還朝，勑集朝賢議其事。

translations.literal: Mid-Wuping, Shou returned to court; an edict gathered eminent ministers to deliberate the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Mid-Wuping, Shou returned to court; an edict gathered eminent ministers to debate the question.

sentences.zh: 休之立議從天保為限斷。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi proposed fixing the founding boundary at the Tianbao era.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi argued that the founding era should be fixed at Tianbao.

sentences.zh: 魏收存日，猶兩議未決。

translations.literal: While Wei Shou still lived, the two positions remained unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: While Wei Shou still lived, the two positions remained deadlocked.

sentences.zh: 收死後，便諷動內外，發詔從其義。

translations.literal: After Shou died he stirred sentiment inside and outside the court until an edict was issued adopting his view.
translations.idiomatic: After Shou died he stirred opinion inside and outside court until an edict was issued in his favor.

sentences.zh: 後領中書監，便謂人云：「我已三為中書監，用此何為？

translations.literal: Later, when he again headed the Secretariat, he said to people: "I have already been Secretariat Director three times—what use is this title to me?"
translations.idiomatic: Later, when he again headed the Secretariat, he said: "I have already been secretariat director three times—what do I need this for?"

sentences.zh: 」隆化還鄴，舉朝多有遷授，封休之燕郡王。

translations.literal: When Longhua returned to Ye, many throughout court received new appointments; Xiuzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Longhua returned to Ye, many at court received new appointments; Xiuzhi was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan commandery.

sentences.zh: 又謂其所親云：「我非奴，何意忽有此授。

translations.literal: He also told those close to him: "I am no slave—why should such an appointment suddenly come to me?"
translations.idiomatic: He also told those close to him: "I am no bondsman's son—why should such an honor fall on me out of nowhere?"

sentences.zh: 」凡此諸事，深為時論所鄙。

translations.literal: All such matters were deeply despised in the talk of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Such conduct earned him deep contempt in the talk of the age.

sentences.zh: 休之好學不倦，博綜經史，文章雖不華靡，亦為典正。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi loved learning without tiring, mastered the classics and histories comprehensively; though his writing was not florid, it was canonical and correct.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi loved learning and never tired of it; he mastered the classics and histories broadly; his prose was not ornate, but it was sound and correct.

sentences.zh: 邢、魏殂後，以先達見推。

translations.literal: After Xing and Wei died, he was esteemed as an elder of the former generation.
translations.idiomatic: After Xing Shao and Wei Shou died, he was honored as an elder of the former generation.

sentences.zh: 位望雖高，虛懷接物，為搢紳所愛重。

translations.literal: Though his rank and fame were high, he received people with open humility and was beloved and respected among the gentry.
translations.idiomatic: Though his rank and fame were high, he met others with open humility and was beloved among the gentry.

sentences.zh: 周武平齊，與吏部尚書袁聿修、衛尉卿李祖欽、度支尚書元修伯、大理卿司馬幼之、司農卿崔達拏、秘書監源文宗、散騎常侍兼中書侍郎李若、散騎常侍給事黃門侍郎李孝貞、給事黃門侍郎盧思道、給事黃門侍郎顏之推、通直散騎常侍兼中書侍郎李德林、通直散騎常侍兼中書舍人陸乂、中書侍郎薛道衡、中書舍人高行恭、辛德源、王劭、陸開明十八人同徵，令隨駕後赴長安。

translations.literal: When Zhou conquered Qi in the Wuping era, he was summoned together with eighteen others—including Minister of the Civil Service Yuan Yuxiu, Chamberlain of the Guards Li Zuqin, Minister of Revenue Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Justice Sima Youzhi, Minister of Agriculture Cui Dana, Secretariat Director Yuan Wenzong, Regular Companion and Secretariat Vice Director Li Ruo, Regular Companion and Attendant Cavalier Li Xiaozhen, Attendant Cavalier Lu Sidao, Attendant Cavalier Yan Zhitui, Regular Attendant and Secretariat Vice Director Li Delin, Regular Attendant and Secretariat Drafting Officer Lu Yi, Secretariat Vice Director Xue Daohang, and Secretariat Drafting Officers Gao Xinggong, Xin Deyuan, Wang Shao, and Lu Kaiming—to follow the imperial train afterward to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou conquered Qi in the Wuping era, he was summoned with eighteen others—among them Yuan Yuxiu, Minister of the Civil Service, Li Zuqin, Chamberlain of the Guards, Yuan Xiubo, Minister of Revenue, Sima Youzhi, Minister of Justice, Cui Dana, Minister of Agriculture, Yuan Wenzong, Secretariat Director, and Li Ruo, Li Xiaozhen, Lu Sidao, Yan Zhitui, Li Delin, Lu Yi, Xue Daohang, Gao Xinggong, Xin Deyuan, Wang Shao, and Lu Kaiming—to follow the imperial train to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 盧思道有所撰錄，止云休之與孝貞、思道同被召者，是其誣罔焉。

translations.literal: In something Lu Sidao wrote down he said only that Xiuzhi, Xiaozhen, and Sidao were summoned together—this was his distortion.
translations.idiomatic: In one of Lu Sidao's accounts he named only Xiuzhi, Xiaozhen, and himself as summoned—a deliberate slanting of the record.

sentences.zh: 尋除開府儀同，歷納言、中大夫、太子少保。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office, passed through as Palace Secretary, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and served in turn as palace secretary, Grand Master of Palace Counsel, and junior mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 大象末，進位上開府，除和州刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daxiang era he was advanced to Upper Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and made Governor of He Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Daxiang era he was advanced to Upper Honored Companion of the Sovereign's Office and made governor of He Province.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇二年，罷任，終於洛陽，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the second year of Sui Kaihuang he left office and died at Luoyang, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaihuang he left office and died at Luoyang, aged seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 所著文集三十卷，又撰《幽州人物志》並行於世。

translations.literal: His collected works ran to thirty juan; he also compiled A Record of Notable Men of You Province, both circulated in his day.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to thirty juan; he also wrote A Record of Notable Men of You Province—both circulated in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 子辟強，武平末尚書水部郎中。

translations.literal: His son Bikong, at the end of Wuping, was Bureau Director of Waterways in the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bikong, at the end of Wuping, was bureau director of waterways in the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 辟強性疏脫，無文藝，休之亦引入文林館，為時人嗤鄙焉。

translations.literal: Bikong was by nature careless and unrestrained, without literary accomplishment; Xiuzhi nevertheless had him admitted to the Forest of Literature Hall, to the ridicule and scorn of contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Bikong was careless and unrestrained and had no literary gift; Xiuzhi nevertheless had him admitted to the Forest of Literature Hall, to the scorn of his contemporaries.

sentences.zh: 袁聿修，字叔德，陳郡陽夏人。

translations.literal: Yuan Yuxiu, courtesy name Shude, was a man of Yangxia in Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yuxiu, courtesy name Shude, came from Yangxia in Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 魏中書令翻之子也，出後叔父躍。

translations.literal: He was the son of Fan, Secretariat Director of Wei, and was given in adoption to his uncle Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was the son of Fan, Wei secretariat director, and was given in adoption to his uncle Yue.

sentences.zh: 七歲遭喪，居處禮度，有若成人。

translations.literal: At seven he suffered bereavement; in deportment and ritual observance he was like an adult.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he lost a parent; in deportment and ritual observance he was already like a grown man.

sentences.zh: 九歲，州辟主簿。

translations.literal: At nine he was invited by the province as chief secretary.
translations.idiomatic: At nine the province invited him to serve as chief secretary.

sentences.zh: 性深沉有鑒識，清凈寡欲，與物無競，深為尚書崔休所知賞。

translations.literal: By nature deep and discerning, pure, sparing in desire, without rivalry toward others, he was deeply known and prized by Cui Xiu of the Ministry of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and discerning by nature, pure and sparing in desire, without rivalry toward others, he won the deep regard of Cui Xiu of the Ministry of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 魏太昌中，釋褐太保開府西閤祭酒。

translations.literal: In the Wei's Taichang era he first donned official robes as Libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Grand Tutor's sovereign office.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wei's Taichang era he first entered office as libationer of the Western Pavilion of the Grand Tutor's sovereign office.

sentences.zh: 年十八，領本州中正。

translations.literal: At eighteen he headed the rectification office of his native province.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he headed the rectification office of his native province.

sentences.zh: 尋兼尚書度支郎，仍歷五兵左民郎中。

translations.literal: Soon he was concurrently Director of the Revenue Section in the Ministry and also passed through as director in the military and left-people sections.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was concurrently director of the revenue section and also served in the military and left-people sections.

sentences.zh: 武定末，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: At the end of Wuding he was Court Scribe to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Wuding he was court scribe to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 天保初，除太子庶子，以本官行博陵太守。

translations.literal: At the start of Tianbao he was appointed Household Companion to the Heir Apparent and acted as Administrator of Boling with his former title.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Tianbao he was made household companion to the Heir Apparent and acted as administrator of Boling under his existing title.

sentences.zh: 數年，大有聲績，遠近稱之。

translations.literal: Within a few years he achieved great reputation and record; near and far praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years he won a strong reputation; near and far praised his record.

sentences.zh: 八年，兼太府少卿，尋轉大司農少卿，又除太常少卿。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was concurrently Vice Director of the Imperial Storehouse; soon transferred to Vice Director of the Grand Granary, then appointed Vice Director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was concurrently vice director of the Imperial Storehouse; he soon transferred to vice director of the Grand Granary, then became vice director of the Grand Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 皇建二年，遭母憂去職，尋詔復前官，加冠軍、輔國將軍，除吏部郎中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Huangjian he left office on his mother's death; soon an edict restored his former posts, advanced him to General Who Conquers Barbarians and General Who Assists the State, and appointed him Bureau Director of the Civil Service Section.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Huangjian he left office to mourn his mother; soon an edict restored his posts, advanced him to General Who Conquers Barbarians and General Who Assists the State, and made him bureau director of the civil service section.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷司徒左長史，加驃騎大將軍，領兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Left Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education, advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and concurrently acted as Imperial Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to left chief clerk of the Minister of Education, advanced to General-in-Chief of the Valiant Cavalry, and concurrently acted as imperial censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 司徒錄事參軍盧思道私貸庫錢四十萬娉太原王乂女為妻，而王氏已先納陸孔文禮娉為定，聿修坐為首僚，又是國之司憲，知而不劾，被責免中丞。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Lu Sidao of the Minister of Education privately borrowed four hundred thousand from the treasury to betroth the daughter of Wang Yi of Taiyuan, but the Wang family had already accepted betrothal gifts from Lu Kongwenli; Yuxiu, sitting as chief staff officer and also the state's judicial overseer, knew yet did not impeach, and was reprimanded and removed as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Lu Sidao of the Minister of Education privately borrowed four hundred thousand from the treasury to betroth Wang Yi's daughter of Taiyuan, though the Wangs had already accepted betrothal gifts from Lu Kongwenli; Yuxiu, as chief staff officer and the state's judicial overseer, knew and did not impeach; he was reprimanded and stripped of the censorate.

sentences.zh: 尋遷秘書監。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Secretariat Director.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 天統中，詔與趙郡王叡等議定五禮。

translations.literal: During Tiantong an edict ordered him with the Prince of Zhao commandery Rui and others to deliberate and fix the Five Rites.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiantong an edict ordered him, with the Prince of Zhao commandery Rui and others, to deliberate and fix the Five Rites.

sentences.zh: 出除信州刺史，卽其本鄉也，時人榮之。

translations.literal: He went out as Governor of Xin Province—that being his native commandery—and people of the time counted it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: He went out as governor of Xin Province—his native commandery—and men of the time counted it an honor.

sentences.zh: 為政清靖，不言而治，長吏以下，爰逮鰥寡孤幼，皆得其歡心。

translations.literal: His government was pure and tranquil; without many words he brought order; from senior officials down to widows, orphans, and the young, all gave him their goodwill.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was pure and tranquil; without many words he brought order; from senior officials down to widows, orphans, and children, all gave him their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 武平初，御史普出過詣諸州，梁、鄭、兗、豫疆境連接，州之四面，悉有舉劾，御史竟不到信州，其見知如此。

translations.literal: At the start of Wuping censors went out in force touring the provinces; Liang, Zheng, Yan, and Yu bordered one another on all four sides of Xin Province, and everywhere there were denunciations—but no censor ever reached Xin Province; such was the esteem in which he was held.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wuping censors toured the provinces in force; Liang, Zheng, Yan, and Yu lay on every side of Xin, and denunciations arose on all fronts—yet no censor ever reached Xin Province; such was the regard in which he was held.

sentences.zh: 及解代還京，民庶道俗，追別滿道，或將酒脯，涕泣留連，競欲遠送。

translations.literal: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, commoners and clergy alike thronged the roads to see him off, some bringing wine and dried meat, weeping and lingering, each vying to escort him far.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended and he returned to the capital, commoners and clergy alike filled the roads to see him off, some bringing wine and dried meat, weeping and lingering, each vying to escort him farther.

sentences.zh: 旣盛暑，恐其勞弊，往往為之駐馬，隨舉一酌，示領其意，辭謝令還。

translations.literal: As it was high summer he feared they would wear themselves out; again and again he halted his horse, took a single cup with whoever offered, to acknowledge their feeling, then declined and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: It was high summer, and he feared they would weary themselves; again and again he halted his horse, took a single cup from whoever offered one to acknowledge their feeling, then begged them to turn back.

sentences.zh: 還京後，州民鄭播宗等七百餘人請為立碑，斂縑布數百疋，托中書侍郎李德林為文以紀功德。

translations.literal: After he returned to the capital, more than seven hundred provincials led by Zheng Bozong asked that a stele be erected for him; they raised several hundred bolts of silk and cloth and entrusted Vice Director of the Secretariat Li Delin to compose the text recording his merit and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: After he reached the capital, more than seven hundred provincials led by Zheng Bozong asked that a stele be raised for him; they collected several hundred bolts of silk and cloth and asked secretariat vice director Li Delin to compose the inscription recording his merit.

sentences.zh: 府省為奏，勑報許之。

translations.literal: The provincial and central offices memorialized upward; an edict replied granting permission.
translations.idiomatic: The provincial and central offices memorialized; an edict granted permission.

sentences.zh: 尋除都官尚書，仍領本州中正，轉兼吏部尚書、儀同三司，尚書尋卽真。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Minister of Justice while still heading his native rectification office; he was transferred to concurrently serve as Minister of the Civil Service and Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and soon his ministry post became regular.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made Minister of Justice while still heading his native rectification office; he was transferred to concurrently serve as Minister of the Civil Service and Honored Companion of the Three Special Ranks, and soon his ministry post became regular.

sentences.zh: 聿修少平和溫潤，素流之中，最有規檢。

translations.literal: Yuxiu from youth was mild and gentle, warm in manner; among those of plain family background he was the most exact in observance and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuxiu was mild and warm in manner; among men of plain family stock he was the most exact in observance and restraint.

sentences.zh: 以名家子歷任清華，時望多相器待，許其風監。

translations.literal: As the son of an eminent house he held one brilliant post after another; men of reputation widely regarded him with esteem and credited his judgment of character.
translations.idiomatic: As the son of an eminent house he held one brilliant post after another; men of reputation widely esteemed him and trusted his judgment of character.

sentences.zh: 在郎署之日，值趙彥深為水部郎中，同在一院，因成交友。

translations.literal: In his days in the bureau offices Zhao Yanshen served as Bureau Director of Waterways in the same courtyard; they became fast friends.
translations.idiomatic: In his days in the bureau offices Zhao Yanshen was director of the waterways section in the same courtyard; the two became close friends.

sentences.zh: 彥深後被沙汰停私，門生藜藿，聿修猶以故情存問來往。

translations.literal: Later Yanshen was culled and suspended, his disciples scattered like wild greens; Yuxiu still, out of old friendship, kept up inquiries and visits.
translations.idiomatic: Later Yanshen was culled and suspended, his disciples scattered like wild greens in winter; Yuxiu still kept up inquiries and visits out of old friendship.

sentences.zh: 彥深任用，銘戢甚深，雖人才無愧，蓋亦由其接引。

translations.literal: Yanshen employed him; inscribed restraint ran very deep. Though his talent was without reproach, this too owed to Yanshen's introduction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Yanshen took him up; Yuxiu remembered it with deep restraint. His talent needed no apology, yet even that owed to Yanshen's hand on the ladder.

sentences.zh: 為吏部尚書以後，自以物望得之。

translations.literal: After he became Minister of Personnel, he held that he had won the post by public esteem.
translations.idiomatic: Once he was Minister of Personnel, he believed he had earned the post by what the world thought of him.

sentences.zh: 初，馮子琮以僕射攝選，婚嫁相尋，聿修常非笑之，語人云：「馮公營婚，日不暇給。

translations.literal: At first Feng Zicong as Vice Director concurrently handled selections; marriage alliances followed one upon another. Yuxiu often mocked him, telling people: "Master Feng arranges marriages and has not a spare day.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Feng Zicong, as vice director, had also run the selection office; wedding matches came one after another. Yuxiu often laughed at him and said to others, "Master Feng brokers marriages—his days have no spare hour."

sentences.zh: 」及自居選曹，亦不能免，時論以為地勢然也。

translations.literal: " When he himself held the selection office, he could not escape it either; opinion held it was the nature of the post.
translations.idiomatic: " When he himself sat in that office, he could not escape the same; the talk of the time said it was the terrain of the post."

sentences.zh: 在官廉謹，當時少匹。

translations.literal: In office he was honest and careful; few in his day could match him.
translations.idiomatic: In office he was scrupulous and careful; few in his day could stand beside him.

sentences.zh: 魏、齊世，臺郎多不免交通餉遺，聿修在尚書十年，未曾受升酒之饋。

translations.literal: In Wei and Qi times, terrace gentlemen often could not avoid traffic in gifts and presents; Yuxiu spent ten years in the Masters of Writing and never once accepted so much as a cup of wine in tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Qi, secretariat gentlemen seldom escaped gifts and favors; Yuxiu served ten years in the Masters of Writing and never took even a cup of wine as a gift.

sentences.zh: 尚書邢邵與聿修舊款，每於省中語戲，常呼聿修為清郎。

translations.literal: Minister Xing Shao and Yuxiu were old friends; in the ministry they would banter in jest and often called Yuxiu "Clear Gentleman."
translations.idiomatic: Minister Xing Shao and Yuxiu were old intimates. In the ministry they traded jokes, and Shao often called Yuxiu "Clear Gentleman."

sentences.zh: 大寧初，聿修以太常少卿出使巡省，仍命考校官人得失。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daning, Yuxiu went out as Vice Director of the Grand Ceremonials on an inspection tour, and was also ordered to assess officials' merits and faults.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Daning year, Yuxiu left the capital as vice director of the Grand Ceremonials on a circuit inspection, and was told to weigh officials' gains and failures.

sentences.zh: 經歷兗州，時邢邵為兗州刺史，別後，遣送白綢為信。

translations.literal: Passing through Yan Province, Xing Shao was then governor of Yan; after they parted, Shao sent white silk as a token.
translations.idiomatic: His route took him through Yan province, where Xing Shao was governor. After they had parted, Shao sent white silk as a courtesy.

sentences.zh: 聿修退綢不受，與邢書云：「今日仰過，有異常行，瓜田李下，古人所慎，多言可畏，譬之防川，願得此心，不貽厚責。

translations.literal: Yuxiu returned the silk and would not accept it, writing to Xing: "Today I pass above—an unusual circumstance. 'Melon field, plum beneath'—the ancients were wary of it; many words bring fear, like holding back a river. I pray you take this heart and do not lay heavy blame on me.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxiu sent the silk back and wrote Xing: "Today I pass through your ground—an uncommon walk. The ancients warned of the melon field and the plum tree; many words are to be feared, like a river you must bank. Take this as my heart, and do not lay a heavy charge on me."

sentences.zh: 」邢亦忻然領解，報書云：「一日之贈，率爾不思，老夫忽忽，意不及此，敬承來旨，吾無間然。

translations.literal: " Xing also gladly understood, replying: "A gift of a single day, offered without thought; this old man in his haste did not reach so far. I respectfully receive your meaning—between us there is no gap.
translations.idiomatic: " Xing took it gladly and answered: "A gift of a single day, sent without thinking it through—this old man, in his haste, never got that far. I accept your meaning; between us there is no gap."

sentences.zh: 弟昔為清郎，今日復作清卿矣。

translations.literal: You, younger brother, were once Clear Gentleman; today you are Clear Minister again.
translations.idiomatic: " You were once Clear Gentleman; today you are Clear Minister again."

sentences.zh: 」及在吏部，屬政塞道喪，若違忤要勢，卽恐禍不旋踵，雖以清白自守，猶不免請謁之累。

translations.literal: When he was in the Ministry of Personnel, government was blocked and the Way was lost; to go against powerful interests would bring disaster in no time. Though he kept himself by integrity, he still could not escape the burden of petition visits.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ministry of Personnel the age was corrupt; to cross those who mattered was to invite ruin overnight. He kept his hands clean, yet even so could not shake off the drag of callers bearing gifts.

sentences.zh: 齊亡入周，授儀同大將軍、吏部下大夫。

translations.literal: When Qi fell he entered Zhou, appointed Colonel-in-Ordinary of the First Rank and Vice Minister in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi fell he entered Zhou and was made colonel-in-ordinary of the first rank and vice minister in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 大象末，除東京司宗、中大夫。

translations.literal: Late in the Elephant reign he was made Director of the Imperial Clan at the Eastern Capital, vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Elephant reign he was made director of the imperial clan at the Eastern Capital, with vice-minister rank.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，加上儀同，遷東京都官尚書。

translations.literal: At the opening of Sui Kaihuang he was given additional Grand Colonel-in-Ordinary of the First Rank and transferred to Minister of the Capital at the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui opened under Kaihuang he was raised to grand colonel-in-ordinary of the first rank and moved to minister of the capital at the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 東京廢，入朝，又除都官尚書。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Capital was abolished he entered court and was again made Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: When the Eastern Capital was abolished he came to court and was again made Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 二年，出為熊州刺史。

translations.literal: In the second year he went out as governor of Xiong Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he went out as governor of Xiong province.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died, at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 子知禮，武平末儀同開府參軍事。

translations.literal: His son Zhi Li, late in Wuping, was Colonel-in-Ordinary and staff officer of an establishment that opened the government.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi Li, late in Wuping, was colonel-in-ordinary and staff officer of an establishment that opened the government.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇中，侍御史，歷尚書民部考功侍郎。

translations.literal: Under Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, and served through Minister of the Household for the People and Vice Director of Merit Assessment.
translations.idiomatic: Under Sui Kaihuang he was attendant censor, then passed through minister of the household for the people and vice director of merit assessment.

sentences.zh: 大業初，卒於太子中舍人。

translations.literal: Early in Daye he died in the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he died while serving as attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：崔彥玄奕世載德，不忝其先；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Cui Yanxuan bore virtue through generations and did not shame his forebears;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Cui Yanxuan carried virtue down the generations and did not disgrace his line;

sentences.zh: 盧詹事任俠好謀，志尚宏遠；

translations.literal: Lu the Chamberlain loved knights-errant and liked stratagems; his aims were broad and far;
translations.idiomatic: Lu Qian, as chamberlain, loved bold companions and good counsel; his aims ran wide and long;

sentences.zh: 陽僕射位高望重，鬱為時宗；

translations.literal: Yang the Vice Director stood high in rank and heavy in esteem, flourishing as the age's pillar;
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xiuzhi the vice director stood high in rank and weight in the world's eyes, a pillar of his time;

sentences.zh: 袁尚書清明在躬，以器能見任；

translations.literal: Yuan the Minister was clear within himself and trusted for his capacity;
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Yuxiu the minister kept clarity in his own person and was trusted for what he could do;

sentences.zh: 與陽斐、盧潛並朝之良也。

translations.literal: together with Yang Fei and Lu Qian they were the court's fine men.
translations.idiomatic: with Yang Fei and Lu Qian they were the court's best men.

sentences.zh: 有齊季世，權歸佞幸，賴諸君維持名教，不然則拔本塞源，裂冠毀冕，安可道哉！

translations.literal: In Qi's late age power fell to flatterers; these gentlemen alone upheld name and teaching—otherwise roots would have been torn up and sources stopped, caps torn off and regalia destroyed; how could it be spoken of!
translations.idiomatic: In Qi's last days power went to flatterers; only these men held up rites and learning. Without them the roots would have been pulled and the source dammed, caps torn off and regalia trampled—who could even name such an age?

sentences.zh: 贊曰：惟茲數公，心安寵辱，不夷不惠，坐鎮流俗。

translations.literal: Appraisal: Only these several lords—hearts at ease with favor and disgrace, neither harsh nor indulgent—sat firm over the drifting manners of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Praise: These men alone—hearts at ease with favor and disgrace, neither harsh nor soft—sat like weights on the age's drifting customs.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年十一月、第一版《北齊書》為本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
translations.idiomatic: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972) as the base for collation.
